title: OneDrive and SharePoint: single hero link for file and folder sharing
summary: The briefing accurately describes the hero link, rollout, licensing context and PowerShell controls. Hold for one missing qualification: the legacy site-default admin-centre route does not work for Teams private or shared channel sites, where Microsoft requires PowerShell.

claims.claim: The change introduces the hero link for Microsoft 365 file and folder sharing.
claims.quote: At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

claims.claim: Each OneDrive and SharePoint item has one primary sharing link, called the hero link.
claims.quote: In OneDrive and SharePoint, each item has one hero link.

claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's audience without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: A hero link allows users to share a single link for an item, then change the audience and permissions for that link without needing to create a new URL.

claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's permissions without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: Changing the scope or permission doesn't create a new URL.

claims.claim: Add people remains a separate way to share by granting direct access.
claims.quote: Users can share an item with specific people or security groups through Add people. This action grants direct access to the item.

claims.quote: We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default.

claims.claim: The new sharing experience applies when users copy a link.
claims.quote: Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL.

claims.quote: No action is required before rollout. Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.

claims.claim: The notice affects all users who share or manage files and folders across SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft 365 sharing.
claims.quote: Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365. Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

claims.claim: The single-link model replaces creating and resending new links when access requirements change.
claims.quote: The hero link consolidates sharing controls into a single link that can be updated after it has been shared, reducing the need to create and resend new links when access requirements change.

claims.claim: Anyone with the link permits use without signing in.

claims.claim: Selecting a broad hero link audience does not make the content searchable for everyone.
claims.quote: Selecting this scope doesn't grant organization-wide access or make the item available in search or Copilot for everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: Selecting a broad hero link audience does not make the content accessible through Copilot for everyone.
claims.quote: Selecting this scope doesn't make the content globally searchable or accessible through Copilot, or grant access to everyone.

claims.claim: Access and searchability through a broad link depend on the recipient receiving and redeeming it.
claims.quote: A person must receive and redeem the link by selecting it before the shared content becomes searchable for them. Access through the link is established when a recipient redeems it.

claims.claim: An item shared through Add people can appear in search for selected users and security group members, subject to permissions.
claims.quote: The item can appear in search results and is accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to their permissions.

claims.claim: An item shared through Add people is accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to permissions.
claims.quote: The item can appear in search results and is accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to their permissions.

claims.quote: At this scope, the link works for people who already have access, such as through a direct permission, a group, or the parent folder or site. It grants no additional access.

claims.claim: Reducing effective access requires changing each source granting a higher permission.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -DefaultMainLinkScope <OnlyPeopleAdded|Organization|Anyone> sets a site's default hero link audience.
claims.quote: The default audience for main links used in sharing. Applies to all items at the root of the document library. Only audience scope is set by this parameter. The default effective value is `OnlyPeopleAdded`.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for setting a site's default hero link audience.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center default audience tenant site UI PowerShell; DefaultMainLinkScope admin center. Opened shareable-links, Set-SPOSite and default-sharing-link pages. Only PowerShell is documented for the hero default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-wide default hero link audience control is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint DefaultMainLinkScope hero link tenant-wide setting UI default audience site collection; hero link tenant default admin control. Read MC1454378, shareable-links and Set-SPOTenant; no tenant-wide hero-audience control found.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists no main link parameter as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint DefaultMainLinkScope hero link tenant-wide setting; searched the fetched Set-SPOTenant reference for MainLink, main link and hero. No matching parameter or setting was present.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Set-SPOSite valid-parameter list for OneDrive for Business omits DefaultMainLinkScope, leaving the documentation in conflict with the notice.
claims.quote: For OneDrive for Business site collection, the only valid parameters are Identity, AllowDownloadingNonWebViewableFiles, AllowEditing, ConditionalAccessPolicy, DefaultLinkPermission, DefaultSharingLinkType

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Set-SPOSite valid-parameter list for Groups site collections omits DefaultMainLinkScope, so the page does not promise support there.
claims.quote: For Groups site collection, the only valid parameters are Identity, AllowSelfServiceUpgrade, DefaultLinkPermission, DefaultSharingLinkType, DenyAddAndCustomizePages, DisableCompanyWideSharingLinks

claims.claim: MC1454378 says DefaultMainLinkScope can configure the default at SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.

claims.claim: MC1454378 lists OnlyPeopleAdded, the default, and Organization as supported values, whereas the reference also lists Anyone.
claims.quote: Supported values are: OnlyPeopleAdded (default); Organization

claims.claim: The Anyone DefaultMainLinkScope value requires anonymous links to be allowed at tenant level.
claims.quote: Anyone is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level.

claims.claim: An Anyone default falls back to the next most restrictive value if Anyone links are disabled for the site.
claims.quote: If Anyone is selected but the site has Anyone links disabled, the effective default falls back to the next most restrictive value.

claims.claim: DefaultMainLinkScope applies to all items at the root of the document library.
claims.quote: The default audience for main links used in sharing. Applies to all items at the root of the document library. Only audience scope is set by this parameter.

claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Policies > Sharing > External sharing reaches the organisation-level external sharing control.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Policies, and then select Sharing. Under External sharing, set your sharing level for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -SharingCapability <value> configures the organisation's external sharing level.
claims.quote: SharingCapability: Determines what level of sharing is available for OneDrive and SharePoint sites. The valid values are: ExternalUserAndGuestSharing; Disabled; ExternalUserSharingOnly; ExistingExternalUserSharingOnly.

claims.claim: A site's sharing setting must be the same as or more restrictive than the organisation's setting.
claims.quote: Each site has its own sharing setting that you can set independently, though it must be at the same or more restrictive setting as the organization.

claims.claim: The legacy site-default control is reached through Active sites > site > Sharing > Default sharing link type > Same as organization-level setting, without a site-type qualification.
claims.quote: To change the default link type for a Teams private or shared channel site, you must use the Set-SPOSite PowerShell cmdlet.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path, but add to controls[3].note: 'For Teams private or shared channel sites, use Set-SPOSite instead; the admin-centre route does not apply.' This qualification is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/change-default-sharing-link.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -DefaultSharingLinkType <value> sets the site's legacy default sharing link type.
claims.quote: DefaultSharingLinkType: The default link type for the site collection. To be replaced by DefaultShareLinkScope. PARAMVALUE: None | AnonymousAccess | Internal | Direct

claims.claim: The site-level DefaultMainLinkScope default is the only documented hero-link-specific administrator control in the researched material.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link admin controls default permission folder automatic permission updates block; hero link controls admin settings; DefaultMainLinkScope admin center. Read shareable-links, Set-SPOSite, Set-SPOTenant and MC1454378. No additional hero-specific admin control.
